'''Silvana Botti''' is a full professor for Theory of Excited States of Integrated Solid State Systems at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Botti, Silvana • Fakultät für Physik und Astronomie |url=https://www.physik.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/Professuren/prof-dr-botti-silvana/ |access-date=2024-01-12 |website=Fakultät für Physik und Astronomie |language=de-DE}}</ref> She is an expert in the development of first-principles methods for electronic excitations and methods for theoretical [[spectroscopy]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2020-06-20|title=Condensed Matter Theory|url=https://www.acp.uni-jena.de/botti.html|access-date=2020-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620160846/https://www.acp.uni-jena.de/botti.html|archive-date=20 June 2020}}</ref>

== Education and professional life ==
She did her PhD at the [[University of Pavia]] in 2002.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2020-06-20|title=AG – Marques / Uni. Halle|url=https://www.tddft.org/bmg/people.php?oid=5040305|access-date=2020-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620160525/https://www.tddft.org/bmg/people.php?oid=5040305|archive-date=20 June 2020}}</ref> After her PhD, she was a [[Marie Curie Fellowship|Marie-Curie Fellow]] at the [[University of Paris-Saclay]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2020-06-20|title=About the Editors {{!}} npj Computational Materials|url=https://www.nature.com/npjcompumats/about/editors?proof=trueJul&draft=journal|access-date=2020-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620165013/https://www.nature.com/npjcompumats/about/editors?proof=trueJul&draft=journal|archive-date=20 June 2020}}</ref> She was also appointed CNRS Research Scientist there in 2004.<ref name=":3" /> In 2008, she moved to [[University of Lyon]] where she habilitated in 2010.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> In 2014, she became a full professor for physics at the [[University of Jena]].<ref name=":1" /> Her research group was a member of the European Theoretical Spectroscopy Facility.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-20|title=Research Team Leaders {{!}} etsf|url=https://www.etsf.eu/index.php/research-teams|access-date=2020-06-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620161533/https://www.etsf.eu/index.php/research-teams|archive-date=20 June 2020}}</ref> Since 2023, she has been a full professor for Theory of Excited States of Integrated Solid State Systems at [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref name=":4" />

== Research ==
Her research focuses on theoretical spectroscopy and the development of first-principles methods for electronic excitations based on (time-dependent) [[density functional theory]] and many-body perturbation theory.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2020-06-20 |title=IFTO-Forschung Gruppe Botti |url=http://www.ifto.uni-jena.de/index.php?page=topic-1_1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620155422/http://www.ifto.uni-jena.de/index.php?page=topic-1_1 |archive-date=20 June 2020 |access-date=2020-06-20}}</ref><ref name=":1"/> She edited the book "First Principles Approaches to Spectroscopic Properties of Complex Materials".<ref>{{Cite book|editor-last1=Di Valentin |editor-first1=Cristiana |editor-last2=Botti |editor-first2=Silvana |editor-last3=Cococcioni |editor-first3=Matteo |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/1062330736 |title=First principles approaches to spectroscopic properties of complex materials|date=22 September 2016|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-662-51178-7|oclc=1062330736}}</ref> She is an associate editor of ''[[npj Computational Materials]]''.<ref name=":3" /> Botti was part of an international research collaboration on a silicon-based direct bandgap light emitter, which was announced to be the "Breakthrough of the Year" by Physics World in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-17|title=Silicon-based material with a direct band gap is the Physics World 2020 Breakthrough of the Year|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/silicon-based-material-with-a-direct-band-gap-is-the-physics-world-2020-breakthrough-of-the-year/|access-date=2021-01-07|website=Physics World|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fadaly |first1=Elham M. T. |last2=Dijkstra |first2=Alain |last3=Suckert |first3=Jens Renè |display-authors=2 |date=2020-04-08 |title=Direct-bandgap emission from hexagonal Ge and SiGe alloys |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2150-y |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=580 |issue=7802 |pages=205–209 |doi=10.1038/s41586-020-2150-y |pmid=32269353 |issn=1476-4687|arxiv=1911.00726 |bibcode=2020Natur.580..205F }}</ref>
